Main.sentence: ___E:Elections U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elections_in_the_United_States)___ were held in the United States on November 2, 2010, in the middle of ___E:Democratic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States))___ President ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ 's first term. ___E:Republicans U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States))___ ended unified Democratic control of ___E:Congress U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Congress)___ and the presidency by winning a majority in the ___E:House of Representatives U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives)___ and gained seats in the ___E:Senate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate)___ despite Democrats holding Senate control.
Republicans gained seven seats in the Senate (including a special election held in January 2010) but failed to gain a majority in the chamber.
In the House of Representatives, Republicans won a net gain of 63 seats, the largest shift in seats since the ___E:1948 elections U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1948_United_States_elections)___ .

In state elections, Republicans won a net gain of six gubernatorial seats and flipped control of twenty state legislative chambers, giving them a substantial advantage in the redistricting that occurred following the ___E:2010 United States census U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_United_States_census)___ .
The election was widely characterized as a ___E:"Republican wave" election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wave_elections_in_the_United_States)___ , and President Obama called it "a shellacking."

The heavy Democratic losses in 2010 were mainly attributed to the passing of the ___E:Affordable Care Act U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Affordable_Care_Act)___ along with a poor economic recovery from the ___E:Great Recession U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Recession)___ and large budget deficits.
This marked the first election since 1858 that yielded a Republican-controlled House and a Democratic-controlled Senate.
Candidates and voters in 2010 focused on national economic conditions and the economic policies of the Obama administration and congressional Democrats.

Attention was paid to public anger over the ___E:Wall Street bailout U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emergency_Economic_Stabilization_Act_of_2008)___ signed into law by President ___E:George W. Bush U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush)___ in late 2008. Voters were also motivated for and against the ___E:sweeping reforms of the health care system U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patient_Protection_and_Affordable_Care_Act)___ enacted by Democrats in 2010, as well as concerns over tax rates and record deficits.
At the time of the election, unemployment was over 9%, and had not declined significantly since ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ had become president.

Further eroding public trust in Congress were a series of scandals that saw Democratic representatives ___E:Charlie Rangel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlie_Rangel)___ and ___E:Maxine Waters U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maxine_Waters)___ , as well as Republican senator ___E:John Ensign U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Ensign)___ , all accused of unethical or illegal conduct in the months leading up to the 2010 election. [citation needed]

Immigration reform had become an important issue in 2010, particularly following the passage of ___E:Arizona Senate Bill 1070 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arizona_SB_1070)___ , officially known as the Support Our Law Enforcement and Safe Neighborhoods Act. The Act greatly enhanced the power of Arizona's law enforcement agencies to investigate the immigration status of suspected illegal immigrants and to enforce state and national immigration laws. [citation needed] The Act also required immigrants to carry their immigration documentation on their person at all times.

Its passage by a Republican-led legislature and its subsequent and very public signing by ___E:Jan Brewer U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jan_Brewer)___ , the Republican ___E:Governor of Arizona U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_of_Arizona)___ , ignited protests across the Southwest and galvanized political opinion among both pro-immigration Latino groups and Tea Party activists, many of whom supported stronger measures to stem illegal immigration. [citation needed]

The passage of the controversial ___E:Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patient_Protection_and_Affordable_Care_Act)___ also contributed to the low approval ratings of Congress, particularly Democrats, in the months leading up to the election. [citation needed] Many Republicans ran on a promise to repeal the law, and beat incumbent Democratic opponents who had voted in favor of the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act. [citation needed]

On January 19, 2010, a special election was also held for the Class I seat in ___E:Massachusetts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massachusetts)___ , as a result of the death of incumbent Senator ___E:Ted Kennedy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Kennedy)___ .
Republican ___E:Scott Brown U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_Brown_(politician))___ won the seat.

The 34 seats in the ___E:United States Senate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate)___ ___E:Class III U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Classes_of_United_States_Senators)___ were up for election.

In addition, the Class I/II seats held by appointed Senators ___E:Ted Kaufman U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Kaufman)___ of ___E:Delaware U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delaware)___ , ___E:Kirsten Gillibrand U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kirsten_Gillibrand)___ of ___E:New York U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_(state))___ , and ___E:Carte Goodwin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carte_Goodwin)___ of ___E:West Virginia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Virginia)___ were contested in ___E:special elections U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/By-election)___ on the same day. Republicans picked up six seats, but Democrats retained a majority in the Senate.
All 435 voting seats in the ___E:United States House of Representatives U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives)___ were up for election.

Additionally, elections were held to select the ___E:delegates U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delegate_(United_States_Congress))___ for the ___E:District of Columbia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/District_of_Columbia)___ and four of the five ___E:U.S. territories U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_insular_area)___ .

The only seat in the House not up for election was that of the ___E:Resident Commissioner of Puerto Rico U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Resident_Commissioner_of_Puerto_Rico)___ , who serves a four-year term and faced election in ___E:2012 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_elections,_2012)___ .

Republicans won the nationwide popular vote for the House of Representatives by a margin of 6.8 points  and picked up 63 seats, taking control of the chamber for the first time since the ___E:2006 elections U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_United_States_elections)___ .

This represented the largest single-election shift in House seats since the ___E:1948 elections U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections,_1948)___ and the largest midterm election shift since the ___E:1938 elections U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections,_1938)___ .

The only seat Democrats flipped without unseating a Republican was Delaware's lone House seat, going to former Lt. Governor ___E:John Carney U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carney_(Delaware_politician))___ .
37 state and two territory ___E:United States governors U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor#United_States)___ were up for election.
Republicans picked up a net of six state governorships; Democrats won control of five governorships previously controlled by Republicans, but Republicans took 11 governorships.

In many states where the following positions are elected offices, voters elected state executive branch offices (including ___E:Lieutenant Governors U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lieutenant_governor_(United_States))___ (though some will be voted for on the same ticket as the gubernatorial nominee), ___E:Secretary of state U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secretary_of_state_(U.S._state_government))___ , ___E:state Treasurer U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_Treasurer)___ , ___E:state Auditor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_Auditor)___ , ___E:state Attorney General U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_Attorney_General)___ , state Superintendent of Education, Commissioners of ___E:Insurance U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insurance_commissioner)___ , Agriculture or, Labor, etc.) and state judicial branch offices (seats on ___E:state Supreme Courts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_Supreme_Court)___ and, in some states, state appellate courts).
Republicans made substantial gains in state legislatures across the nation.

Twenty chambers flipped from Democratic to Republican control, giving Republicans full control of eleven state legislatures and control of one chamber in Colorado, Iowa, and New York.   Additionally, Republicans gained enough seats in the Oregon House of Representatives to produce a 30-30 party split, pushing Democrats into a power-sharing agreement that resulted in the election of two "co-speakers" (one from each party) to lead the chamber.
Republicans gained a net of 680 seats in state legislative races, breaking the previous record of 628 flipped seats set by Democrats in the post-Watergate elections of 1974.

Six states saw both chambers switch from Democrat to Republican majorities: Alabama (where the Republicans won a majority and a trifecta for the first time since 1874), Maine (for the first time since 1975 and a trifecta for the first time since 1965), Minnesota (for the first time since 1915 in partisan elections and 1973 in non-partisan elections), New Hampshire, North Carolina (for the first time since 1896), and Wisconsin.
In addition, by picking up the lower chambers in Indiana, Ohio, Michigan, Montana [a] and Pennsylvania, Republicans gained control of both chambers in an additional five states.
Furthermore, Republicans picked up one chamber from Democrats in Colorado, Iowa, and New York to split control in those states.
They expanded majorities in both chambers in Texas, Florida, and Georgia.
